Deficient insulin secretion following surgery is an endocrine pancreatic disorder; exocrine pancreatic damage is not specified.
Congenital structural defect of the upper eyelid; associated syndromic abnormalities are not intrinsic to the isolated concept.

Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; olfactory bulb aplasia in 4/6 and hyposmia in 5/10 establish common neurologic loss of function. Renal and hearing abnormalities lack qualifying frequency.
Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia with hyperammonemia; persistent developmental disability in 1/1 assessed and atrial septal defect in 1/1. Organ-frequency evidence is limited by tiny samples.

Benign female reproductive tract epithelial-stromal tumor, represented by ovarian mucinous adenofibroma; no covered organ origin established.
X-linked skeletal dysplasia with punctate cartilage calcification and a metabolic classification. Skin and ocular disease vary by subtype and are not established across most of the umbrella.

Malignant germ cell tumor arising in the central nervous system during childhood.
Inherited platelet adhesion defect with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding; mucocutaneous bleeding does not establish separate skin or gastrointestinal disease.
Defective UV damage repair causes cutaneous photodamage; chronic ocular surface injury, including keratitis and eyelid damage, affects a majority. Neurologic degeneration is atypical of group C.
Isolated sperm structural abnormalities and male infertility; no endocrine dysfunction or other covered organ disease.
Sarcoma arising in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ; mesenchymal histology alone does not establish musculoskeletal origin.
Defined by neurodevelopmental abnormalities, with microcephaly in 80–99%. Other documented organ abnormalities are occasional; frequent hand differences lack clear functional damage.
Structural narrowing of the vertebral canal. Pain or claudication alone does not establish lasting neural damage; separately diagnosed radiculopathy or myelopathy is not added.
